name: Ministry of Unification NKMap FastApi Gazetteer
publisher: 통일부 북한정보포털 (Ministry of Unification North Korea Information Portal)
description: Hidden REST search endpoint powering South Korea's official North Korea GIS portal, containing over 304,000 geocoded North Korean places, facilities, factories, mines, schools, transit stops, and historical landmarks. Coordinates are provided in Korea 2000 Central Belt (EPSG:5186) alongside detailed administrative hierarchy (province, city/county, district/ri) and rich sectoral attributes.
coverage: 1945–present; entire Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK)
last_updated_evidence: Vite SPA frontend bundle index-BtHHbpDp.js built in late 2023/2024; backend data updated with recent administrative divisions and industrial plant listings.
license: 공공누리 제1유형 (Open Government License Type 1 - attribution required)
presentation: Trapped inside a slow, heavy Korean-only web GIS portal (NKMap) backed by VWorld WebGL plugin. English OSINT researchers have never discovered this backend JSON API.
build_idea: The backbone gazetteer for our entire Atlas: convert all 304,598 points from EPSG:5186 to WGS84 and build an instant autocomplete search engine for every facility, mine, railway station, and collective farm in North Korea.
notes: Verified live via probe_nkmap_api.py. Querying wildcard returns total=304,598. Specific queries confirm 2,042 factories, 1,669 railway stations, 752 mines, 364 coal mines, and 622 educational institutions.

name: Ministry of Unification Defector Arrivals & Demographic Time Series
publisher: 통일부 (Ministry of Unification)
description: Official quarterly and annual statistics of North Korean escapees arriving in South Korea from before 1998 through 2026. Details arrivals by gender, age groups, year, and cumulative totals (over 34,000 individuals).
last_updated_evidence: Live webpage includes 2025 preliminary totals and 2026 monthly updates with female ratio metrics.
presentation: Rendered as a single static HTML table on a Korean-language government website; lacks interactive charts, regional filtering, or export options.
build_idea: An interactive defector arrivals timeline chart showing annual spikes (Arduous March aftermath, peak in 2009 at 2,914 arrivals), the dramatic border closure drop during COVID-19, and the 2024–2026 rebound.
notes: Verified live via HTTP request. Cumulative male arrivals stand at 9,593 while female arrivals account for over 72% of all defectors.

name: Defector Origin Province and Socioeconomic Demographics
publisher: 통일부 / 남북하나재단 (Korea Hana Foundation via data.go.kr)
description: Comprehensive statistical breakdown of North Korean defectors by pre-defection province of origin (2008–present), pre-defection occupation, educational attainment, and age structure. Reveals that over 58% originate from North Hamgyong Province, ~16% from Ryanggang Province, and ~9% from South Hamgyong Province.
coverage: 2008–2026; DPRK provinces (Hamgyong-buk, Ryanggang, Hamgyong-nam, Pyongyang, etc.)
last_updated_evidence: Data.go.kr catalog metadata shows modification timestamp 2026-09-30 (alternateName: 통일부_북한이탈주민 주요 현황_20250630).
presentation: Published as downloadable Korean PDF reports on data.go.kr; numbers are trapped in tabular layouts rather than downloadable CSVs or GeoJSON.
build_idea: A province-level choropleth map of North Korea displaying defector origin density: visually explaining why border regions (Hoeryong, Musan, Onsong, Hyesan) dominate escape demographics compared to interior provinces.
notes: Verified via data.go.kr API and catalog metadata. Catalog JSON confirms data covers pre-defection origin provinces, pre-defection occupations, and settlement indicators.

name: KOSIS North Korea Statistics Portal
publisher: 국가데이터처 (Statistics Korea / National Data Agency)
description: South Korea's centralized macro-statistical repository on North Korea across 14 categories, including Bank of Korea North Korean GDP/GNI estimates, population census and fertility rates, agricultural output (crop production by year), mineral output, trade with China and Russia, and energy generation.
last_updated_evidence: Portal updated following BOK 2025 NK GDP report and Statistics Korea annual North Korea Major Indicators publication.
presentation: Comprehensive but fragmented across dozens of sub-tables; navigation requires navigating Korean ActiveX/modernized tree-lists with awkward iframe viewers.
build_idea: Clean, interactive comparison charts of North vs. South Korea development over time: GDP per capita trajectory, energy production collapse, infant mortality rate, and trade dependency on China.
notes: Verified live via probe_kosis_nk.py. Covers 14 thematic classifications including population, health, agriculture, mining, foreign trade, and national accounts.

name: Asia Press / Rimjin-gang North Korea Underground Market Price Surveys
publisher: アジアプレス・ネットワーク (Asia Press International Osaka / Tokyo)
description: Bi-weekly and monthly field price surveys conducted via undercover reporting networks inside North Korean cities (Hyesan, Chongjin, Pyongsong, Musan). Tracks real street prices of white rice, corn, pork, diesel, gasoline, alongside unofficial black market exchange rates for USD/KPW and CNY/KPW.
last_updated_evidence: Survey series 'price-survey-10' published September 2026 detailing hyperinflation, price spikes, and household living cost models.
license: All rights reserved (fair use summary / citation permissible)
presentation: Longform journalism articles in Korean and Japanese with embedded tables; historical data is dispersed throughout individual dispatch articles without a unified API or CSV download.
build_idea: A living North Korea Inflation & Market Tracker: price curves of food staples (rice vs. corn price gap is the prime famine indicator) and unofficial street exchange rate depreciation vs USD and RMB.
notes: Verified live via probe_asiapress_rimjingang.py. Dispatches through September 2026 detail the post-pandemic electronic payment mandate and grain monopoly struggles.

name: Soseikai Specific Missing Persons Database (Suspected Japanese Abductees)
publisher: 特定失踪者問題調査会 (Specific Missing Persons Investigation Commission of Japan)
description: Detailed investigative registry of 276+ Japanese citizens suspected of abduction to North Korea. Each case record provides full name, exact date of disappearance, geocodable coastal location (prefecture, city, coastline), age at disappearance, occupation, physical characteristics, and investigative narrative.
coverage: 1948–present; coastal Japan (Niigata, Fukui, Ishikawa, Tottori, Akita, Kagoshima, etc.) and abroad
last_updated_evidence: Site archives actively updated; RSS feed at /archives/missing/feed/ verifies continuous maintenance and recent case revisions.
presentation: WordPress catalog with paginated individual victim cards. Never before mapped geographically in English as an interactive coastal intelligence visualization.
build_idea: A coastal abduction map of Japan: pinpointing every disappearance point along the Sea of Japan coast, correlated with North Korean spy ship operations, coastal radar blind spots, and infiltration routes.
notes: Verified live via probe_japan_abductees.py. Fetched individual profiles confirming structured Japanese fields: 氏名, 失踪年月日, 生年月日, 性別, 当時の年齢, 失踪場所, 失踪状況.

name: Cabinet Secretariat Official Abductee and Case Dossiers
publisher: 内閣官房 拉致問題対策本部 (Headquarters for the Abduction Issue, Cabinet Secretariat of Japan)
description: Official Japanese government dossier of the 17 state-recognized abduction victims (Megumi Yokota, Yaeko Taguchi, Kaoru Hasuike, etc.) and 12 distinct abduction incident operations executed by North Korean agents along the Japanese coast and in Europe.
last_updated_evidence: Official 2026 summary pamphlet published January 2026 (202601pamphlet_jp.pdf); event logs updated September 2026.
presentation: Presented as educational text and downloadable PDF brochures; clean narrative but lacks interactive mapping or geospatial linkage.
build_idea: Incorporate official state-recognized abduction incidents into the Atlas timeline, linking victims with the clandestine training camps where they were forced to instruct DPRK spies in Japanese language and customs.
notes: Verified live via probe_japan_abductees.py. Detailed incident summaries include the Ushutsu case, Niigata coastline kidnapping, Fukui siblings abduction, and European lures.

name: National Police Agency Abduction Suspects & ICPO Red Notices
publisher: 警察庁 警備局 (National Police Agency of Japan, Security Bureau)
description: Criminal investigative records of DPRK state intelligence operatives with international arrest warrants issued via Interpol (ICPO) for kidnapping Japanese nationals, including Sin Kwang-su, Kim Se-ho, and Kim Myong-suk. Includes operation dates, methods (clandestine vessels, forged passports), and victim identities.
last_updated_evidence: Reiwa 6 (April 2024) case status update noting warrant expiration/confirmation of death for co-conspirator Kim Kil-uk.
presentation: Legacy HTML pages encoded in UTF-8 with BOM; official police wanted posters with photos, aliases, and operational descriptions.
build_idea: Perpetrator profiles linked to coastal abduction sites: showing the operative network of North Korean Bureau 35 / Reconnaissance General Bureau that conducted maritime infiltrations.
notes: Verified live via probe_japan_abductees.py. Contains exact operational records such as the June 1980 abduction of Tadaaki Hara from Aoshima Beach, Miyazaki Prefecture, onto a spy vessel.

name: Japan MOD Ballistic Missile Launch Press Releases
publisher: 防衛省・自衛隊 (Ministry of Defense of Japan)
description: Continuous real-time military announcements of North Korean ballistic missile launches, published within minutes of detection. Contains precise launch time, launch region in DPRK, trajectory direction, apogee altitude (km), flight distance (km), and splashdown coordinates/bearing relative to Japanese islands and EEZ boundaries.
coverage: 2016–2026; Korean Peninsula & Sea of Japan / Pacific Ocean
last_updated_evidence: Launches tracked continuously through 2026, including August 20, 2026 salvo launch announcement (2026/08/20d.html).
presentation: Individual HTML press releases with follow-ups (速報 -> ミサイル落下推定情報 -> 続報). Rich technical telemetry that is rarely parsed systematically into English GIS formats.
build_idea: Direct feed to update our /missiles map with official Japan MOD radar telemetry: verifies launch time, flight distance, apogee, and impact coordinates against CNS/USFK estimates.
notes: Verified live via probe_japan_defense.py. Multiple 2026 launches documented with exact parameters (e.g. August 20, 2026 launch at 17:04: apogee 90km, range 320km, northeast heading).

name: Japan MOD Maritime Sanctions Evasion (Ship-to-Ship Transfers) Surveillance
publisher: 防衛省・自衛隊 (Ministry of Defense of Japan)
description: Declassified surveillance records and photographic evidence gathered by JMSDF patrol aircraft and international partners (Australia, Canada, Netherlands, New Zealand) monitoring illegal ship-to-ship transfers (瀬取り) by sanctioned North Korean oil tankers.
last_updated_evidence: Releases published through 2026 tracking foreign patrol deployments and illegal transfer incidents.
presentation: Archive with annual HTML subpages and high-resolution PDF reconnaissance dossiers including aerial photographs, vessel names, IMO numbers, and nautical coordinates.
build_idea: A Maritime Sanctions Evasion layer: plot exact coordinates of confirmed illegal mid-sea fuel transfers in the East China Sea, showing vessel names (CHON MA SAN, NAM SAN 8) and partner flags.
notes: Verified live via probe_japan_defense.py. Confirms specific tanker incident PDFs with IMO numbers (8660313, 8122347, 8610461, 7303803, etc.).

name: Japan Coast Guard North Korean Wooden Drift Boat Statistics
publisher: 海上保安庁 (Japan Coast Guard)
description: Annual statistical compilation of North Korean wooden fishing vessels and ghost ships (漂流・漂着木造船) washing ashore along the Sea of Japan coast (Hokkaido, Aomori, Akita, Yamagata, Niigata, Ishikawa, Fukui, Shimane). Records total vessels, survivor rescues, and deceased recovered.
last_updated_evidence: Annual 海上保安レポート (Coast Guard Annual Report) summarizes drift vessel statistics and Yamato Bank patrol interventions.
presentation: Published in chapters of the annual Maritime Safety White Paper (海上保安レポート); tables present yearly vessel arrivals and prefectural distributions.
build_idea: A Sea of Japan Ghost Ships map layer displaying coastal drift arrival clusters: highlighting the deadly human toll of Pyongyang's winter squid fishing quotas and diesel fuel shortages.
notes: Verified via JCG records and web grounding. Over 800+ North Korean wooden vessels documented since 2013, with peak years in 2017–2019 exceeding 100-200 vessels annually.

name: Chongryon Uri Hakkyo School Directory
publisher: 在日本朝鮮人総聯合会 (General Association of Korean Residents in Japan - Chongryon)
description: Complete official directory of all pro-Pyongyang ethnic Korean schools (ウリハッキョ) in Japan, including Korea University (小平市), high schools, middle schools, and elementary schools. Each record contains exact Japanese postal codes, street addresses, and contact numbers across every Japanese prefecture.
coverage: Current; nationwide Japan (Tokyo, Kanagawa, Osaka, Kyoto, Aichi, Hyogo, Fukuoka, etc.)
last_updated_evidence: Chongryon official portal education directory reflects current school merges and operating campuses.
presentation: Clean tabular HTML in UTF-8 on the official Chongryon Japanese website; addresses are readily geocodable using standard Japanese geocoders.
build_idea: A diaspora geography layer: map all Chongryon schools and institutions in Japan, illustrating their historic relationship with Pyongyang funding, repatriation alumni, and local municipal subsidy debates.
notes: Verified live via probe_chongryon.py. Confirms entries like 朝鮮大学校 (東京都小平市小川町1-700), 東京朝鮮中高級学校 (東京都北区十条台2-6-32), and regional primary schools.

name: Chongryon Prefectural Headquarters Directory
publisher: 在日本朝鮮人総聯合会 (General Association of Korean Residents in Japan)
description: Complete institutional directory of Chongryon's 47 prefectural headquarters across Japan, with postal codes, exact street addresses, and phone numbers.
last_updated_evidence: Live directory on Chongryon site listing active prefectural offices.
presentation: Static HTML table with complete postal addresses from Hokkaido to Okinawa.
build_idea: Map the formal organizational network of Pyongyang's de facto embassy and consulate network across Japan.
notes: Verified live via probe_chongryon.py. Lists Tokyo HQ (台東区東上野), Kanagawa HQ (横浜市神奈川区鶴屋町), etc.

name: Niigata Port North Korea Repatriation Project (帰国事業) Historical Data
publisher: 新潟市歴史博物館 (Niigata City History Museum) / 日本赤十字社 (Japanese Red Cross Society)
description: Historical voyage manifests and passenger statistics for the 1959–1984 'Paradise on Earth' repatriation program that transported 93,340 Zainichi Koreans and Japanese spouses from Niigata Port to Chongjin on Soviet vessels (Kril'on, Tobolsk).
coverage: 1959–1984; Niigata Port, Japan to Chongjin / Wonsan, DPRK
last_updated_evidence: Niigata City museum documentation and Japanese Red Cross archival publications.
presentation: Archival documentation, historical photographs, and ship passenger registers housed in Niigata municipal records.
build_idea: A dedicated migration corridor map from Niigata Port to Chongjin: tracing the 187 repatriation voyages, the Niigata Red Cross reception center, and the tragic fate of returnees sent to internal exile and camps.
notes: Verified via historical archives and Japanese Red Cross statistics. Total repatriated: 93,340, including 6,839 Japanese spouses/dependents.

name: KINU North Korean Human Rights Information Platform
publisher: 통일연구원 (Korea Institute for National Unification - KINU)
description: Specialized digital portal aggregating South Korea's official academic research on North Korean human rights: penal facilities (정치범수용소 / 구금시설), abductees and POWs (국군포로, 납북자), overseas forced labor, and original DPRK legal codes.
last_updated_evidence: Platform launched and updated in 2025/2026 with new categorized board modules and legal statute indexes.
presentation: Modernized portal with structured thematic taxonomy, though deep reports are delivered as attached PDF publications.
build_idea: A structured Human Rights Violation Reference: linking Atlas detention locations to KINU's legal analysis and verified defector testimony databases.
notes: Verified live via probe_kinu_whitepaper.py. Sub-boards specifically categorize detention facilities (/nkhr/board/index.do?code=R4n4BVkkuo2), food rights, and original DPRK documents.

name: KINU Annual White Paper on Human Rights in North Korea
publisher: 통일연구원 (Korea Institute for National Unification)
description: The authoritative annual human rights white paper series published by the South Korean government's premier unification think tank since 1996. Features extensive statistical annexes on political prison camps (Kwanliso 14, 15, 16, 25), correctional facilities (Kyohwaso), public executions, and defector survey samples.
last_updated_evidence: Report archive includes White Paper 2025 (idx 132082) with 2026 edition in active compilation.
presentation: Comprehensive 500+ page annual books with tables; available as PDF downloads on the KINU report portal.
build_idea: Extract KINU's historical tables on detention center operations and testimony counts into structured JSON data powering camp timeline views.
notes: Verified live via probe_kinu_whitepaper.py. Category 46 contains all annual white papers since 1996.

name: Ministry of Unification Report on North Korean Human Rights
publisher: 통일부 북한인권기록센터 (Center for North Korean Human Rights Records, Ministry of Unification)
description: Landmark official South Korean government human rights reports (published publicly in 2023, 2024, and 2025) compiling verified testimony from over 1,600 defectors on public executions, forced repatriation reception centers (집결소), secret police detention, and Reactionary Ideology and Culture Rejection Act crackdowns.
coverage: 2016–2026; DPRK cities, counties, and border repatriation points
last_updated_evidence: Annual release cycle by Ministry of Unification; 2024 and 2025 reports published in Korean with summary English editions.
presentation: Polished official publication available as full PDF and printed volume; contains incident case studies with specific county-level names.
build_idea: Geolocate incident case studies: public trial locations, execution firing ranges, and repatriation processing hubs (Dandong-Sinuiju, Tumen-Namyang).
notes: Verified via Unikorea portal. First publicly released under the Yoon administration, shifting Center records from classified status to public release.

name: Ministry of Unification Daily North Korea Weather Dataset
publisher: 통일부 (Ministry of Unification via data.go.kr)
description: Daily meteorological observations across North Korea's principal geographic regions: Sonbong, Samjiyon, Chongjin, Chunggang, Pungsan, Kanggye, Sinuiju, Anju, Hamhung, Pyongyang, Haeju, Kaesong, and Wonsan. Records temperature, rainfall, and weather status.
last_updated_evidence: Data.go.kr dataset page confirms modification date 2026-09-29.
presentation: Standard CSV file download on Public Data Portal; updated continuously.
build_idea: Live weather overlay for our map: show daily temperatures, rainfall, and freezing conditions across North Korea (crucial for monitoring Yalu/Tumen river freezing during winter defection seasons).
notes: Verified live via probe_data_go_kr.py. Dataset ID 15039464.

name: KMA 27 North Korea WMO Synoptic Weather Stations
publisher: 기상청 (Korea Meteorological Administration - KMA)
description: Official South Korean meteorological monitoring network for 27 World Meteorological Organization (WMO) surface observation stations across North Korea. Provides daily mean temperature, high/low, precipitation, wind speed, and snow depth for Pyongyang, Samjiyon, Hyesan, Kanggye, Chongjin, Sinuiju, Wonsan, etc.
last_updated_evidence: Weather portal provides live daily observation data updated multiple times per day.
presentation: Interactive regional map and tabular view on weather.go.kr; historical time-series downloadable via data.kma.go.kr.
build_idea: Historical climate and drought/flood tracker: visualize extreme drought and flood seasons in North Korea that precipitate agricultural crop failures and food crises.
notes: Verified live via probe_kma_nk_weather.py. Station IDs include 108 (Pyongyang), 136 (Samjiyon), 137 (Hyesan), 131 (Chongjin), 143 (Kanggye).

name: Ministry of Unification North Korea Key Figures (Elites) OpenAPI

name: Ministry of Unification North Korea Historical Chronicle OpenAPI

last_updated_evidence: Data.go.kr dataset updated 2026-09-30.
presentation: Public REST API providing machine-readable schedule objects.
build_idea: A propaganda programming dashboard: analyze what percentage of daily state TV is devoted to leader idolization, military achievements, or foreign news.

name: National Library Information Center on North Korea Catalog
publisher: 국립중앙도서관 북한자료센터 (Information Center on North Korea, National Library of Korea)
description: South Korea's premier institutional archive of original North Korean primary materials: over 110,000 cataloged books, periodicals (로동신문, 민주조선, 근로자), maps, elementary/secondary textbooks, propaganda posters, and government legal codes.
last_updated_evidence: Center operates continuously with new material acquisitions and digitized holdings.
presentation: Web catalog interface allowing search by author, publication year, publisher (Pyongyang Foreign Languages Publishing House, Workers' Party of Korea Publishing House), and classification.

name: NGII North Korea Topographic & Spatial Data Platform
publisher: 국토지리정보원 (National Geographic Information Institute - NGII)
description: South Korea's national surveying agency repository of North Korean spatial data: 1:25,000 and 1:50,000 digital topographic maps, satellite orthophotos, road/rail networks, and administrative boundary vectors produced using national satellite imagery.

name: National Assembly Research Service North Korea Policy Reports
publisher: 국회입법조사처 (National Assembly Research Service - NARS)

publisher: KBS (Korean Broadcasting System 남북교류협력단)

presentation: Clean shapefile and GeoJSON format ready for QGIS or MapLibre consumption.

name: kp-to-ko Cultural Language Converter
publisher: july0785 (GitHub)
description: Open-source Python linguistic utility that converts North Korean Munhwa-eo (문화어) orthography, phonology (initial consonant rule / 두음법칙 variances: 례외 -> 예외, 로동 -> 노동), and DPRK-specific vocabulary back to standard South Korean.
last_updated_evidence: GitHub commit history and release tags.
presentation: Lightweight Python library and CLI tool.
